problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=x{y}^{2},\,y(1)=2.
$$

Earlier part 1:

feedback.worked_solution:
Our tangent line approximation is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =4x-2.\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $y(\frac{3}{2})$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=\frac{3}{2}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}y(\frac{3}{2}) & ≈L(\frac{3}{2}) \\  & =4\cdot (\frac{3}{2})-2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
